attributes.name: Ministry of Technology (TechMin)
attributes.short_description: Building a better student life, one tool at a time!
attributes.description:
We're Ashoka's in-house product team. Basically, a bunch of students who got tired of complaining about campus life and decided to just fix it ourselves.

TechMin is where you learn by building. We design, build, and launch the tools people on campus actually use, not ideas that live and die in a group chat. You've probably already used something we made without even realizing it was us: Sem Planner and Trajectory Planner (so you can plan your semester and degree without crying over a spreadsheet), Pool a Cab, SG Compose, Mail Room Digitization (no more sprinting to the mail room to check if your order has arrived), and plenty more we can't wait for Ashoka to discover.

And here's the best part: you don't need to know how to code to join us. Seriously. We need people who can design, write, strategize, manage projects, hunt down bugs, or just have really good ideas about what's broken and how to fix it. If you can think, you can build with us.

Join TechMin and you're on a team, owning a real product from "wouldn't it be nice if..." to something students actually open on their phones. You'll pick up product thinking, design chops, and dev skills along the way, sure. But mostly, you'll get to fix the thing that annoyed you last semester, for literally everyone on campus.

We're students building for students. Come make Ashoka smarter, smoother, and a lot less annoying.
attributes.induction_description:
Long story short, we're inducting for 3 roles - the Creative Director, the Technical Product Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer. We don't care about your resume. We care about the itch to fix something that's been bothering you. To organise something that just seems so inefficient. To always stand out in everything that you do. If that describes you, then let's face it - we need you. And you need a place where you can prove to yourself, and to Ashoka what you're capable of.
Before we say more about the roles, know this - more than (probably) any other body at Ashoka, Techmin functions literally like a startup. A place where you understand constraints, solve problems, and experiment like never before. This year, we want to double down on this. These roles don't just sound like startup roles, they basically are. And the best part? You get to tell us what you want out of the role. If this interests you, here's what you can apply for:
  1. Creative Director: Lead our Growth & GTM, and Workshops & Events verticals. This is NOT a social media HOD role. Though we can't guarantee that reel making and ideation won't be a part of the job, the main responsibility of the Creative Director is to figure out a disruptive, bold, and unique positioning for Techmin and our products. If you've ever wanted to develop a brand from scratch, and give a peek of the inside of your mind to Ashoka, this is your chance. Apply here: https://techmin.fillout.com/creative-director
  2. Technical Product Manager: For the person already mentally redesigning that one broken campus process nobody else will touch. Half-baked ideas walk in, working products walk out. You're the oven. You don't need to know to write code - you just need to know how to solve problems. If you want a close-to-life emulation of how product development at a Startup functions, this is your chance. Apply here: https://techmin.fillout.com/tech-pm
  3. Chief Financial Officer: You don't just maintain a spreadsheet. You make real decisions, work under immense constraints, and figure out jugaadu ways to make Techmin work. And that's not all. You're going to maintain our inventory - containing very high stakes items, with very dynamic needs. If you're the kind of person to flex how well managed your expenses have been, this is your real test. Apply here: https://techmin.fillout.com/cfo

attributes.name: Ashoka Political Science Society
attributes.short_description: The Ashoka Political Science Society fosters dialogue, debate, and research, exposing students to the real world of politics beyond the classroom. It is organised into six departments: the Ashoka Political Science Review, publishing the society’s annual journal; the Ashoka Project on Election Analysis, producing Ranneeti newsletter with insights on elections and voting trends; the Events Department, hosting talks, panels, workshops, and mixers; the Marketing Department, shaping the society’s identity through design, communication, and campaigns; the Outreach Department, building collaborations and connecting students with opportunities; and the Tech Department, providing the technical support needed for smooth functioning. Together, they create a space for Ashokans to explore ideas, collaborate, and engage critically with politics.
attributes.description:
The Ashoka Political Science Society is an academic forum committed to fostering intellectual engagement, critical inquiry, and collaborative learning among students passionate about politics. It facilitates discussions that aim to open minds and expose students to the real world of politics—beyond textbooks—by encouraging dialogue, debate, and diverse perspectives. The society provides a platform for exploring political ideologies, analysing global trends, and cultivating a deeper understanding of socio-political systems.

The society is organised into six departments, each contributing to this mission. The Ashoka Political Science Review (APSR) is the official journal, where students edit, review, and publish high-quality papers each year. The Ashoka Project on Election Analysis (APEA) produces Ranneeti, a newsletter featuring accessible analysis of elections, voting trends, and political behaviour in India and beyond. The Events Department plans and hosts panels, talks, and workshops with academics, practitioners, and policymakers, along with community activities like the PolSci Mixer. The Marketing Department handles design, communication, and social media campaigns to showcase the society’s work and reach a wider audience. The Outreach Department builds collaborations with other societies, engages with faculty and practitioners, and makes career opportunities more accessible for students. Finally, the Tech Department provides the technical support needed for smooth functioning, whether for events, systems, or troubleshooting.

Together, these six departments create an inclusive and intellectually stimulating environment for students to connect, collaborate, and meaningfully engage with the discipline of political science.
attributes.induction_description:
We are excited to announce that inductions for general membership of the Ashoka Political Science Society (APSS) are officially open! This is your chance to be part of a vibrant community where ideas thrive.

Here are the teams you can be part of:

  • APSR (Ashoka Political Science Review): Coordinate peer reviews, lead the editorial team, and ensure high-quality editing to bring out a strong final journal issue each year.
    Apply here
  • Marketing: Shape the Society’s identity by handling design, communication, and social media. From engaging posts to campaigns, you’ll ensure APSS reaches and inspires the wider student body.
    Apply here
  • APEA (Ashoka Project on Election Analysis): Work on APSS’ flagship newsletter Ranneeti and contribute to sharp, accessible analysis of elections, voting trends, and political behavior in India and beyond.
    Apply here
  • Events: Conceptualize, plan, and host discussions, panels, and talks with academics, practitioners, and policymakers. You’ll be creating the spaces where important conversations come alive. You'll also get to organise fun events like the PolSci Mixer. 
    Apply here
  • Outreach: Build connections outside Ashoka. From collaborations with student societies to engaging with faculty and practitioners, Outreach keeps APSS visible and well-connected. The outreach team also makes career opportunities accessible for Ashokans. 
    Apply here
  • Tech: Provide the technical backbone for the Society — whether it’s managing systems, supporting events, or troubleshooting. (We’ll be honest, we really need you, because most of us are pol sci majors ).
    Apply here

At APSS, the only prerequisite to join is passion — a willingness to contribute, collaborate, and be part of something larger than yourself. No matter your major or background, if you’re curious and committed, we’d love to have you on board.

attributes.name: Anime Club
attributes.short_description: The Anime Club at Ashoka University is a community for students who love anime and want to explore Japanese culture. Our goal is to create a space for fans to connect and introduce more people to anime through events, discussions, and screenings. This year, we’ve hosted events like Halloweeb, a Halloween-themed gathering with screenings and fun activities, and Anime Mixer, where participants enjoyed anime games and art and even a fun Symposium. We also organize weekly Fridays4Anime.to screenings, showing classics like Boy and the Heron and Akira. A standout event we organize every year is BudgetCon, our flagship anime festival, which is our version of ComicCon on a budget. This event brings the campus to life with cosplay, gaming zones, stalls featuring merchandise and food, and activities like anime bingo and photobooths.\nBudgetCon is a highlight for anime fans and a great way for others to experience something new. Through these events, the Anime Club continues to foster a space where people can come together to share their love for anime and engage with Japanese culture.
attributes.description:
The Anime Club at Ashoka University is a dynamic and inclusive community designed specifically for students who share a deep appreciation for anime and are interested in exploring the fascinating world of Japanese culture. Our mission is to create an inviting space where anime enthusiasts can come together to connect, learn, and introduce others to the amazing world of anime through a range of engaging events, thoughtful discussions, and exciting screenings. We aim to create a sense of belonging where both long-time fans and newcomers alike can unite over their shared love for anime.

Throughout the year, we organize and host a variety of fun and engaging events that celebrate both anime and the culture surrounding it. One such event is Halloweeb, our Halloween-themed gathering that brings together the excitement of the spooky season with the joy of anime. At this event, participants enjoy screenings of anime films with a Halloween twist, along with a variety of activities like cosplay contests, themed snacks, and anime trivia. Another fan-favorite is Anime Mixer, an event where participants can engage in anime-themed games, admire beautiful fan art, and participate in an interactive symposium where they discuss all things anime, from the latest trends to deep dives into classic works.

In addition to these, we also run Fridays4Anime.to, a weekly screening event that gives students the chance to experience classic anime films and series. Popular screenings have included iconic works such as The Boy and the Heron and Akira, giving fans an opportunity to revisit these beloved titles or experience them for the first time in a communal, interactive setting.

However, the crown jewel of the Anime Club’s events is undoubtedly BudgetCon—our flagship anime festival. This annual event, which serves as Ashoka University’s very own version of Comic-Con on a budget, transforms the campus into a lively celebration of anime, manga, and Japanese pop culture. BudgetCon features a mix of exciting activities, including cosplay competitions, gaming zones, stalls offering anime merchandise and delicious food, as well as fun interactive activities like anime bingo and photobooths for attendees to capture the unforgettable moments. It's an event where anime fans from all backgrounds come together to celebrate their passion, and it offers an opportunity for newcomers to explore the world of anime in an engaging and accessible way.

Through all these events and activities, the Anime Club continues to nurture a vibrant, inclusive space where students can share their passion for anime, connect with fellow fans, and deepen their understanding of Japanese culture. By fostering such an environment, we aim to ensure that the magic of anime continues to bring people together, spark creativity, and build lasting friendships.

attributes.name: Ashoka Business Club
attributes.short_description: The Ashoka Business Club (ABC) is dedicated to fostering the intersection of business and liberal arts through initiatives that empower students to recognize and build on their strengths. By providing opportunities for holistic growth, ABC helps students from diverse academic backgrounds apply their knowledge and skills to achieve their aspirations. The club aims to inspire a culture of innovation, learning, and collaboration that extends beyond Ashoka’s campus, leaving a lasting impact on the broader community. Through its efforts, ABC strives to prepare individuals to transform their passions into meaningful contributions to society.
attributes.description:
Hosting Distinguished Speakers for Knowledge Sharing:
The Club takes immense pride in organizing events featuring renowned industry experts, offering students invaluable insights into diverse fields. Over the years, we hosted accomplished professionals such as Kartik Kilachand (IIT-IIT.org), Snehil Jain(AVP, HSBC), Sumeet Singh (CMO, Infoedge), Sparsh Agarwal (Co-Founder Dorje Teas, Sharktank S2), Rishabh Gupta (VP, Indiamart) and others. These interactions provided students with firsthand exposure to the expertise and experience of leaders across various domains, broadening their horizons and inspiring their professional aspirations

Professional Excellence and bridging the gap: 
To enable students to apply their newly acquired skills, the Club facilitated internships and client projects with esteemed organizations such as IIM-C, Sadravya Finance, Lynkube, Current, Rungta Advisors and more.

Inter-University Events:
The Business Club also hosts a variety of business simulation competitions encompassing topics like mergers and acquisitions (Monopoly), crisis simulation (Samay-Sya) and more. These competitions see participation from universities across Delhi-NCR. These events offer students a platform to showcase their skills and interact with like-minded individuals.

attributes.name: Ashoka Consulting Club
attributes.short_description: The Ashoka Consulting Club (ACC) is Ashoka University’s premier student-led consulting organization, dedicated to empowering aspiring consultants and delivering high-impact solutions to real-world business challenges. Founded in 2018, ACC bridges the gap between academic rigor and professional expertise through live consulting projects, skill-building workshops, case competitions and networking opportunities. With over 50 members and 6+ years of experience, the club works across industries such as fintech, non-profits, FMCG, and real estate, taking on 6–10 client projects annually. ACC is more than a consulting club—it’s a dynamic, collaborative community where diverse talents converge to solve complex problems and cultivate lifelong skills.
attributes.description:
Founded in 2018, the Ashoka Consulting Club (ACC) has grown into a vibrant, interdisciplinary hub for aspiring consultants and problem-solvers. With over 50 active members and a strong alumni network, the club serves as a training ground and professional launchpad for students passionate about tackling real-world business challenges. Combining Ashoka University’s liberal arts ethos with practical consulting experience, ACC equips its members with the tools to thrive in high-stakes environments.

ACC functions as both an incubator and a consulting practice. Each year, the club takes on 6–10 live projects spanning industries such as fintech, non-profits, real estate, and transportation. Teams of skilled analysts, led by project leaders and advisors, work closely with clients to deliver actionable, high-value solutions. Beyond client engagements, ACC hosts regular skill-building workshops, networking events with alumni and industry experts, and case study sessions to ensure its members remain at the forefront of consulting excellence. In addition to live projects, ACC organizes large-scale events such as case competitions, inter-university collaborations, and speaker sessions that engage the broader student body and cultivates partnerships that amplify its impact.

What sets ACC apart is its sense of community. Members come from diverse disciplines—including Economics, Psychology, Computer Science, and English—creating an interdisciplinary approach to problem-solving. The club fosters camaraderie, collaboration, and a shared commitment to excellence. This strong foundation has enabled ACC alumni to secure positions at marquee firms like McKinsey & Co, Bain, BCG, D.E. Shaw, Dalberg, and AT Kearney and multiple other marquee placements and internships. 

The induction process for the Ashoka Consulting Club (ACC) begins each spring semester with a selection of new analysts. Candidates go through a consulting-style application, interview process and lastly a group discussion that evaluates their problem-solving, communication, and analytical skills.

attributes.name: Ashoka Debating Union
attributes.short_description: The Ashoka Debating Union (ADU) serves as a platform for individuals to come together and engage in various formats of university level debating, fostering an active and organised debating culture on campus. Through debating we sharpen our ability to synthesise ideas and arguments that are both logical and creative. Debating also helps communicate these ideas effectively and convincingly to an audience. To support this culture, the ADU organises several workshops for the members on various aspects of debating and also our flagship inter-varsity parliamentary debate tournament (AUPD). Beyond our own initiatives, we frequently take part in debate tournaments happening all over the world, gaining exposure to diverse perspectives.
attributes.description:
Our Initiatives include: Workshops
Experienced members of the union, who have achieved notable success in tournaments or earned accolades, share their insights through our debating workshops. Each workshop focuses on a specific aspect of debating, such as framing (contextualizing issues to demonstrate the relevance and importance of arguments within a topic), rebuttals, principles, and more. These
sessions aim to enhance members’ skills while fostering collaboration to address and overcome individual weaknesses.


Intra-Varsity Tournament
We organize an annual intra-varsity tournament open to all Ashoka students. Prior to the tournament, we conduct introductory sessions to familiarize participants with the debating format, judging criteria, and other key aspects. This tournament serves as an excellent introduction to university-level debating, allowing students to explore their interest in the activity. Qualifying participants are also invited to join the club. Furthermore, the intra-varsity tournament helps us prepare for the inter-varsity edition by refining our organizational skills.


Ashoka University Parliamentary Debate (AUPD)
The Ashoka University Parliamentary Debate is our flagship inter-varsity tournament. This three-day event brings together contingents and participants from various universities. It features a diverse group of speakers, judges, core adjudicators, and equity officers. Hosting AUPD is a matter of great pride for us, as it enables us to independently promote and sustain the culture of debating.


Mock Debates and Tournaments
Union members are consistently provided with opportunities to participate in offline and online debate tournaments across various formats. With numerous tournaments available, members can form teams and compete in events that align with their interests. Additionally, the union offers a supportive space to organize mock debates, which are instrumental in preparing for tournaments. These mock debates encourage constructive feedback and rigorous training.

attributes.name: Ashoka Fintech Club
attributes.short_description:
The Ashoka Fintech Club aims to create a deeper understanding of the rapidly evolving financial technology sector by providing a dynamic space for learning, discussion, and collaboration. Our goal is to simplify complex terms and concepts such as Blockchain, Open Banking, Regulatory Technology (RegTech), etc. making them accessible to all students, regardless of their academic background. Whether you're studying Finance, Computer Science, Political Science, Philosophy, or from any other field, our goal is to showcase the intersection of these disciplines with fintech and demonstrate its relevance across industries.

Through engaging speaker sessions, panel discussions, and interactive workshops, we plan to bring in experts and thought leaders from various domains to provide insights into the latest trends, challenges, and innovations within the fintech ecosystem. Additionally, we will encourage collaborative projects and assignments that allow students to work on real-world problems, equipping them with relevant skills and practical knowledge.

By nurturing interdisciplinary learning and promoting collaboration among students from diverse academic backgrounds, the club will empower Ashokan students to explore the cross-sections of technology, finance, law, ethics, and policy. This holistic approach will help build a strong foundation for those looking to pursue careers in fintech, entrepreneurship, or any sector influenced by financial technologies.
attributes.description:
The Ashoka Fintech Club is dedicated to fostering a deeper and more comprehensive understanding of the rapidly growing and ever-evolving financial technology (fintech) sector. With the financial landscape undergoing dramatic changes, the club serves as a dynamic and inclusive space that encourages learning, discussion, and collaboration among students. Our central goal is to demystify complex concepts such as Blockchain, Open Banking, Regulatory Technology (RegTech), and many others, making these intricate terms and ideas understandable and accessible to all students, regardless of their academic discipline or background.

Fintech, as a multidisciplinary field, intersects with various domains such as finance, technology, law, policy, and ethics. Whether you’re studying Finance, Computer Science, Political Science, Philosophy, or any other discipline, our club strives to showcase how fintech integrates and interacts with these fields. We believe that the relevance and impact of financial technologies span across industries, and our mission is to illuminate the ways in which each field contributes to and is influenced by the fintech sector.

In pursuit of this, the Ashoka Fintech Club will organize a series of engaging events, including speaker sessions with industry experts, panel discussions on current fintech challenges, and interactive workshops designed to provide hands-on experience and deeper insights. By inviting thought leaders from a wide variety of domains, we aim to offer students a comprehensive view of the latest trends, emerging technologies, and innovative developments in the fintech ecosystem. These events will address the key issues and challenges within the sector, such as regulatory compliance, cybersecurity, digital currencies, and the evolution of financial services.

Furthermore, the club will emphasize collaborative learning through group projects and assignments focused on real-world problems. This approach will allow students to apply their academic knowledge to practical situations, helping them develop critical skills such as problem-solving, teamwork, and creativity. By working on projects that address real-world issues, students will gain hands-on experience and a more nuanced understanding of the challenges and opportunities within fintech. This will also provide them with the skills necessary for careers in fintech, entrepreneurship, and other industries that are increasingly shaped by financial technologies.

The club’s activities will promote an interdisciplinary approach to learning, encouraging collaboration among students from diverse academic backgrounds. This approach will foster an environment where ideas from different fields can merge, resulting in innovative solutions and insights. By exploring the intersections of technology, finance, law, ethics, and policy, the Ashoka Fintech Club will empower students to see the broader picture of fintech’s impact on society.

Our holistic approach ensures that students not only acquire theoretical knowledge but also develop the practical skills required to navigate and excel in the fintech landscape. Whether you’re interested in becoming a fintech entrepreneur, working in a financial institution, or contributing to regulatory policy, the Ashoka Fintech Club will equip you with the foundation and the tools to succeed in a world that is increasingly shaped by financial technology. The club seeks to cultivate a community of curious, innovative, and forward-thinking individuals who are prepared to make a meaningful contribution to the fintech sector and beyond.

attributes.name: Ashoka Health Research Club
attributes.short_description:
AHRC is a one of it’s kind student-led organisation dedicated to leveraging research and innovation to address health issues within the Ashokan community. Mentored by Koita Centre for Digital Health- Ashoka University (KCDH-A), AHRC engages in interdisciplinary approaches to tackle complex health challenges.

AHRC’s core team has two Presidents and Vice Presidents and four major
verticals -
The Projects team, to ensure a smooth internship process and a healthy collaboration
between the KCDH-A supervisors and interns and to promote new student initiatives for health research;
The Inclusions team, to ensure that AHRC does not restrict itself to biology and computer sciences majors only, and respects the true social nature of
the concept of health; 
The Events and Collaborations team to think, and organise events on campus
around health; and the Marketing and social media team for outreach and to take things to a grander stage.
attributes.description:
AHRC has become a space that is collaborative, powerful, and engaging.
We are in touch with almost all major clubs and societies on campus and our media team has developed an interesting engagement with students. We also went on to hold a memorable "5 Days of AHRC" initiative - to spread the word through a series of events, mixers, and competitions and identify more like-minded people who want to be involved with the club. Recently, we also launched a campus-wide application form for gauging interest in interning at KCDH-A research projects, and it is heartening to see we have already received over 40 applications.

The Ashoka Cohort for Health and Well-Being is a research study led by KCDH-A and AHRC members envisioned to understand health through individuals'
responses to lifestyle factors like diet, physical activity, stress etc. This study requires volunteers (students and staff of Ashoka University), to wear sensors like a smartwatch and glucose monitors for a period of time, undergo some site assessments to evaluate their baseline physiology, and record their lifestyle
through logging meals etc.

What is even more interesting is that the study is being built on a predominant digital framework, ordinate with KCDH-A’s mandate of digital health. As AHRC, composed of digital natives, and with promoting health as the mandate, we were major stakeholders and invested in helping KCDH-A with the study. We are currently setting up the logistics for inviting volunteers - keep your eyes open for the call sometime in mid-Nov. Of course, the study is completely voluntary, and signing up for the information sessions or showing interest in participating does not mean you have to. The cohort study christens our first proper research initiative on campus, and we hope to have many more such.

attributes.name: Ashoka Internship Cell
attributes.short_description: The CDO AIC (Career Development Organization - Ashoka Internship Cell) aims to empower Ashokan students by equipping them with essential skills, knowledge, and resources to navigate their professional journeys successfully. We, the AIC, as student representatives of the CDO, focus on fostering a thriving internship culture on campus by organizing skill-building workshops, resume review sessions, and networking events. Our initiatives are designed to prepare students for future internships and career opportunities while sharing the latest internship openings and resources with the Ashokan community. Through collaboration, mentorship, and outreach, we strive to create an environment where every student feels supported and ready to excel in their career endeavors. We conducted 2 major events last semester including the AIC Townhall and a collaboration with WiCS, where we hosted seniors who had done CS-based internships in a panel session interacting with the students and answering their queries.
attributes.description:
The Career Development Organization - Ashoka Internship Cell (CDO AIC) is dedicated to empowering Ashokan students by providing them with the essential skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to navigate their professional journeys with confidence and success. As student representatives of the CDO, we, the Ashoka Internship Cell (AIC), are committed to fostering a vibrant and thriving internship culture on campus. Our primary goal is to prepare students for future internships and career opportunities by offering a wide array of supportive initiatives aimed at developing key competencies.

Our efforts include organizing skill-building workshops, resume review sessions, and networking events designed to equip students with the tools they need to stand out in competitive internship and job markets. These workshops and sessions cover a variety of topics, from crafting an effective resume and preparing for interviews, to developing critical soft skills and understanding industry trends. Through these initiatives, we strive to create an atmosphere where students feel encouraged to actively pursue internships and engage with professional development opportunities.

In addition to the workshops and events, we keep the Ashokan community informed by sharing the latest internship openings, resources, and career development opportunities. We believe that access to current and relevant information is key to empowering students to make well-informed decisions about their professional futures. This constant flow of information ensures that no student feels left behind in the fast-paced, ever-changing professional landscape.

We also emphasize collaboration, mentorship, and outreach as core values within the AIC. By partnering with various student organizations, faculty members, and industry professionals, we create a network of support that guides students toward successful internship placements and career pathways. Our mentorship programs connect students with senior peers and professionals who provide valuable insights and advice, helping them navigate the challenges they may face in their career journey.

Over the past semester, we have successfully organized two major events that have made a significant impact on the Ashokan community. The AIC Townhall, an interactive event, brought together students, faculty, and professionals to discuss various aspects of internships and career development, creating a platform for open dialogue and exchange of ideas. Additionally, we collaborated with the Women in Computer Science (WiCS) group to host a panel session with senior students who had completed Computer Science-based internships. These seniors shared their experiences, answered student queries, and provided invaluable insights into the internship process, helping students better understand what to expect and how to prepare for similar opportunities.

Through these and many other initiatives, the AIC is committed to creating an environment where every Ashokan student feels supported, empowered, and equipped to excel in their career endeavors. We aim to be a continuous source of guidance and inspiration, helping our peers achieve their fullest potential and make meaningful strides toward their professional goals.

attributes.name: Ashoka Investments Club
attributes.short_description:
Ashoka Investments Club (AIC) is the hub for finance enthusiasts at Ashoka University, fostering a culture of financial literacy and investment. Through Bodhi Capital, our student-run investment fund, we focus on the Indian equity markets using a rigorous fundamental analysis approach. Supported by 55 analysts and guided by four portfolio managers, we aim to identify and invest in high-potential opportunities.

This year, we organized several impactful events to strengthen our community and enrich our members. Our speaker sessions featured industry stalwarts like Jatin Khemani, Ramesh Damani, and Harsha Raghavan, culminating in a thought-provoking panel discussion on "The India Growth Story." Additionally, students gained firsthand exposure through office visits to firms like Convergence Capital and Laburnum Capital, as well as site visits to the Exide factory.

Through workshops, networking events, and real-world insights, AIC ensures its members stay at the forefront of the finance world.
attributes.description:
Through a diverse range of activities and initiatives, AIC aims to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and real-world financial practices, empowering students to navigate the complexities of the investment landscape with confidence and competence.

At AIC, students have the opportunity to engage in various enriching experiences that enhance their understanding of the financial world. These include:

Speaker Sessions: AIC hosts insightful sessions with industry leaders, sector experts, and seasoned investors, providing students with unique perspectives on market trends, investment strategies, and career opportunities in finance. These sessions serve as a platform for students to interact with professionals and gain valuable industry insights. Notable speakers from this year included Jatin Khemani, Ramesh Damani, and Harsha Raghavan. The sessions culminated in a thought-provoking panel discussion on "The India Growth Story."

Industry Visits: To offer practical exposure, AIC organizes visits to factories, corporate offices, and other relevant sites, allowing students to witness real-world business operations and better understand the industries they analyze. This year, students visited firms such as Convergence Capital and Laburnum Capital, along with a site visit to the Exide factory. These visits provide firsthand insights into the functioning of various sectors and enhance students' investment acumen.

Knowledge Building: AIC is committed to equipping students with the necessary tools to succeed in finance through workshops, seminars, and discussion sessions. Covering a wide array of topics, from financial markets and valuation techniques to portfolio management and risk assessment, these initiatives ensure that members are well-versed in key financial concepts.

Networking Opportunities: AIC provides a platform for students to connect with like-minded peers, alumni, and industry professionals. The club fosters a collaborative environment where members can share ideas, discuss market trends, and build lasting relationships within the finance community Ashoka Investment Club (AIC)
The Ashoka Investment Club (AIC) is the hub for finance enthusiasts at Ashoka University, fostering a culture of financial literacy and investment across the student body. .

attributes.name: Ashoka Marketing Club
attributes.short_description: The Ashoka Marketing Club (AMC) aims to unite marketing enthusiasts from diverse majors, fostering collaboration and learning through dynamic initiatives.The club aims to be a platform for marketing enthusiasts to showcase their abilities and expand their understanding of the field. With this in mind we have launched a learning community as well to foster a space to keep updated in the marketing field. This year, AMC hosted stellar speaker series featuring industry leaders like Ridhima Manocha (HUL), Ruchira Jaitly (Diageo India), Deepak Goel (DigitallyNext), and Gunjan Arya (OML Entertainment), with each session drawing over 100 attendees. The Externals Department spearheaded impactful brand collaborations, including market research for Necesera, a B2B business deck for Prakhar, and a festive campaign for Tulsi Retail. Meanwhile, the Internals Department showcased creativity through projects like the SDG Expo reels and the Batch Championship, designing engaging visuals and promotional materials that fostered campus-wide collaboration.
attributes.description:
The Ashoka Marketing Club (AMC) has had a vibrant year, combining industry collaborations, creative projects, and engaging events. Its flagship speaker series brought insights from top professionals like Ridhima Manocha (HUL), who discussed FMCG roles, Ruchira Jaitly (Diageo India), who reflected on her journey across top brands, and Deepak Goel (DigitallyNext), who led a session on personal branding. Gunjan Arya (OML Entertainment) added value with a session on digital marketing trends. These events, often held in partnership with other clubs, strengthened AMC’s network and reputation.
The Externals Department excelled in executing meaningful collaborations. For Necesera, the team conducted market research focused on Gen Z preferences and designed a college ambassador program to enhance campus outreach. Prakhar benefited from a strategic B2B business deck that highlighted its unique value propositions, quality standards, and future growth plans. Tulsi Retail’s Diwali campaign integrated creative print ads, auto banners, and social media content for maximum visibility and engagement, blending festive sales with brand-building strategies.
Internally, AMC demonstrated innovation and teamwork in initiatives like the SDG Expo, where impactful reels and visually compelling Instagram content were created to promote sustainability goals. Similarly, the Batch Championship saw the club producing engaging story templates, posters, and banners that fostered campus-wide camaraderie. These diverse activities highlight AMC's commitment to nurturing marketing talent and driving impactful collaborations across platforms.

attributes.name: Khayal
attributes.short_description: Khayal has come into existence with the purpose of creating a culture that makes people not only enjoy movies as final products but also allows them to undergo the enriching experience of creating films, enjoying the entire process of filmmaking, appreciating the efforts that go into making a movie, as well as analyzing, critiquing and appreciating films that we see as audiences and filmmakers.
attributes.description:
Khayal came into place as a club for individuals passionate about filmmaking, whether they are amateurs exploring the craft or experienced creators refining their skills.

The academic year is structured to guide members through various stages of filmmaking. The initial phase focuses on workshops and scriptwriting sessions, where participants work collectively to create scripts. As the year progresses, these scripts are developed into short films and other cinematic projects through a collaborative production process. Alongside production, Khayal hosts events such as film showcases and workshops on specific aspects of filmmaking, including technical and creative skills like editing, sound design, and cinematography.

The club emphasises not just the outcome but also the process of filmmaking, encouraging members to engage with and reflect on the effort and creativity that goes into the craft. They also envision an environment where films are analyzed and critiqued, both as audience members and as filmmakers, enriching participants’ understanding and appreciation of cinema.

The club operates with a defined team structure, including social media members responsible for documenting and sharing the club’s work and finance members ensuring resources are managed effectively to support projects and events.

attributes.name: Rotaract Club of Ashoka University Youth
attributes.short_description: The Rotaract Club of Ashoka University Youth aims to foster community service, social responsibility, and student engagement. Over the years, the club has become a vibrant force in the campus community, spearheading initiatives that resonate with both Ashoka students and surrounding areas like Sonipat and Delhi. The club’s activities range from donation drives, such as clothing, food, and blood donations, to educational initiatives for underprivileged youth, including projects like Project Gyan Aadhar, Project Pankh, Project Badlaav, Project Adhikaar and Project Kalaakar. .Through collaborations with NGOs like Spread Smile Foundation, the Gyan Adhar Welfare Society and Pehchaan Foundation, the club has aimed to make lasting contributions to education, and sustainable practices. These initiatives not only support local communities but also create meaningful experiences for students, reinforcing the importance of empathy and social impact. With a strong volunteer network, the Rotaract Club continues to be recognized for its impact, most recently receiving Ashoka University’s External Engagement Award and being named Exemplary Club  two years in a row for 2023-24 and 2024-25.
attributes.description:
The Rotaract Club of Ashoka University Youth is a thriving student organization committed to fostering a culture of community service, social responsibility, and student engagement. Over the years, the club has become a cornerstone of social impact on campus, bringing together students with a shared passion for making a difference. With a focus on both local communities, such as those in Sonipat and Delhi, and the university itself, the club has launched numerous initiatives that address critical social challenges. These efforts are not only designed to provide direct support to those in need but also to empower students to embrace their role as changemakers.


The club’s activities range from large-scale donation drives—clothing, food, and blood—to long-term educational initiatives aimed at supporting underprivileged youth. Flagship projects like Project Gyan Aadhar focus on providing access to education, while Project Pankh works toward the empowerment of women and girls. Project Badlaav addresses systemic social issues, Project Adhikaar advocates for human rights, and Project Kalaakar nurtures creative talents among the underserved. These projects are not isolated efforts but are supported through strategic collaborations with NGOs such as the Spread Smile Foundation, Gyan Adhar Welfare Society, and Pehchaan Foundation. Together, these partnerships enable the club to create sustainable, long-term impact while fostering a culture of compassion and action within the Ashoka community.


The Rotaract Club’s impact is reflected not only in the success of its initiatives but also in the personal growth of its members. By participating in its projects, students gain firsthand experience in addressing societal challenges, working in teams, and engaging with diverse perspectives. This dual impact—benefiting the community while enriching the student experience—has earned the club significant recognition, including Ashoka University’s External Engagement Award and the title of Exemplary Club two years in a row for 2023-24 and 2024-25. The Rotaract Club exemplifies Ashoka University’s commitment to social responsibility, creating a platform where students can turn empathy into action and contribute meaningfully to the world around them.
attributes.induction_description:
There are four departments within the club, and you may apply to up to 3 departments (fill the form separately for each):

  1. External Engagement: Lead NGO collaborations, ideate and implement curriculums of ongoing projects, design and execute impact projects.
     
  2. Internal Engagement: Foster a culture of service within Ashoka by leading donation drives, fundraising events, student club collaborations, and community engagement both on and off campus. 
     
  3. Finance: Manage sponsorship outreach, fundraising, budgeting, and financial accountability.
     
  4. Social Media & PR: Shape our digital presence, run digital campaigns, offline marketing and amplify RaC AUY’s work to wider audiences.

 

Here’s the link to apply:

attributes.name: Ruhi
attributes.short_description: At Ruhi, we aim to empower the non-teaching staff by teaching spoken and written English, enabling them to communicate independently. Last year, we conducted 20 English classes and distributed over 10,000 pads as part of a donation drive that included an informative session on menstrual health. This year, we focused on fostering inclusivity through engaging events like the SDG Expo, where we highlighted SDG 10 (Reducing Inequalities), and vibrant Diwali celebrations with rangoli, dance, and mehendi stalls. We are also expanding our efforts to include workshops that impart essential skills and promote mutual learning between staff and students.
attributes.description:
At Ruhi, we believe in the power of education and inclusivity to create meaningful change within our community. Our primary goal is to empower non-teaching staff by equipping them with essential skills, such as spoken and written English, enabling them to communicate independently and confidently in various situations. This initiative not only enhances their personal and professional growth but also fosters stronger bonds within our institution by bridging communication gaps.

Last year, we took significant strides toward this mission by conducting 20 dedicated English classes. These sessions were thoughtfully designed to accommodate the unique needs of the participants, blending practical exercises with engaging activities to make learning enjoyable and effective. Witnessing their growing confidence and improved communication skills has been incredibly rewarding and reinforces the importance of this initiative.

In addition to our educational efforts, we are committed to addressing broader social issues. One such endeavor was our impactful donation drive, during which we distributed over 10,000 sanitary pads to those in need. This initiative was coupled with an informative session on menstrual health, aimed at breaking taboos and empowering women with knowledge about their bodies. The positive feedback we received from participants underscored the importance of creating safe spaces for conversations around health and hygiene.

This year, we expanded our focus to include initiatives that foster inclusivity and celebrate diversity. One of our flagship events was the SDG Expo, which highlighted Sustainable Development Goal 10 (Reducing Inequalities). The expo served as a platform to discuss pressing global issues, showcase innovative solutions, and engage the community in meaningful dialogue. Additionally, our vibrant Diwali celebrations brought the community together through traditional activities such as rangoli-making, dance performances, and mehendi stalls. These events were not only a source of joy and connection but also a testament to the value of shared experiences in building a more inclusive environment.

Looking ahead, Ruhi is committed to broadening its impact through workshops that impart essential skills and encourage mutual learning between non-teaching staff and students. These workshops are envisioned as interactive sessions where participants can share knowledge, exchange ideas, and grow together. By creating an environment that values every individual’s contributions, we aim to cultivate a culture of respect, understanding, and collaboration.

attributes.name: Red Brick Words
attributes.short_description: Red Brick Words, Ashoka University’s dynamic writing club, is a welcoming space for wordsmiths and storytellers alike. Since its inception in 2016, the club has evolved from a humble group of poetry enthusiasts into a vibrant community that celebrates diverse forms of writing and their intersections with other disciplines. Our mission is to inspire and nurture creative expression, providing a platform for students to hone their literary skills, share their work, and connect with like-minded peers. From aspiring novelists and passionate poets to adventurous experimenters exploring new writing forms, Red Brick Words welcomes anyone with a love for words to join this journey of self-expression. This semester, we proudly hosted Beyond the Courtroom, an innovative book talk featuring Saurabh Kirpal and Rohin Bhat. This event delved into the fascinating intersection of literature and law, exemplifying our commitment to exploring the multifaceted nature of writing. Looking ahead, we have an array of promising events that we can’t wait to share with the Ashoka community! At Red Brick Words, creativity thrives in a supportive space where every voice is valued, and every story finds its place. Come join us on a journey where creativity takes the lead, and your unique voice truly shines.
attributes.description:
Red Brick Words is Ashoka University’s vibrant writing club—a home for wordsmiths, storytellers, and anyone who finds joy in the power of language. Established with the goal of fostering a love for creative expression, the club provides a platform where students can refine their literary skills, share their work, and build meaningful connections with fellow enthusiasts. Over the years, Red Brick Words has become an important part of Ashoka’s literary culture, inspiring and nurturing a thriving community of writers and dreamers. One of the most beloved aspects of the club is its open-mic nights. These intimate gatherings have become a signature event where students share their poetry, prose, and spoken word performances in a warm and supportive environment. Whether it’s a seasoned writer unveiling a polished piece or someone nervously reading their first poem, these evenings are a celebration of authentic voices and bold self-expression. The sense of camaraderie and encouragement they foster is what makes these events truly special, leaving participants and audience members alike inspired and uplifted.
 

Another highlight of Red Brick Words is The Pocketbook, the club’s annual self-published  collection of student-written poetry. Each year, The Pocketbook explores a new theme,  challenging writers to think creatively and push the boundaries of their craft. The upcoming 7th edition, set to release in Spring 2025, takes on the theme Shifting Sands, delving into ideas of transformation and impermanence. For the first time, it will feature prose and experimental writing alongside poetry, making it the most dynamic edition yet. This labour of love not only celebrates the creative voices of Ashoka but also brings the community closer through the shared experience of writing, publishing, and reading.


At its heart, Red Brick Words is more than just a club—it’s a thriving community where  creativity flourishes, and voices find their place. From hosting events and open-mics to  publishing heartfelt works, the club creates a space for writers and storytellers to explore their passions, take chances, and grow. Whether you’re a seasoned writer, a curious beginner, or someone looking for inspiration, Red Brick Words welcomes you to join a journey of self- expression, collaboration, and celebration of the written word.

attributes.name: The Quizzing Club
attributes.short_description:
"The Quizzing Club’s aim is what it says on the lid - entertaining the Ashoka community through fun and intellectually stimulating quizzes on every single
topic under the sun! We want to create a space where Ashokans of every stripe can spread the trivia-based love about the things close to their heart, and can learn
from each other through a healthy mixture of lateral thinking, QM-quizzer banter and some truly awful puns in the guise of “funny” questions. Quizzing is the one
thing literally everyone can do, because we’re all disgustingly obsessed with something or the other. It is in this spirit of accessibility, and in the pursuit of mind-boggling amounts of communal fun, that the Quizzing Club seeks to create a healthy quizzing culture at Ashoka."
attributes.description:
The Quizzing Club at Ashoka University is a vibrant student-led initiative dedicated to engaging the university community through intellectually stimulating and entertaining quizzes that span a vast array of topics. Embracing the philosophy that everyone harbors a passion for some form of trivia, the club creates an inclusive environment where students can share their unique interests, challenge their minds, and indulge in the playful banter characteristic of quizzing culture. With a commitment to accessibility and communal enjoyment, the club strives to cultivate a robust quizzing culture at Ashoka, encouraging participation from individuals across diverse academic and personal backgrounds.


The club's activities are designed to foster lateral thinking and camaraderie among participants. Signature events like ChakraView, the annual inter-collegiate quizzing festival, attract students from premier institutions nationwide, offering a platform for showcasing knowledge and quick wit. For instance, ChakraView 2019 featured multiple quizzes, including MELA Quiz and Biz-Tech, and was hosted by renowned quizmaster Major Chandrakant Nair, drawing over 100 students from esteemed colleges and schools. In 2022, ChakraView 3.0 was conducted online, reflecting the club's adaptability and commitment to maintaining engagement despite challenges. Additionally, the club has a history of hosting sectional rounds for prominent competitions like the Tata Crucible Campus Quiz, further embedding Ashoka University within the national quizzing circuit.
Beyond large-scale events, the Quizzing Club organizes regular sessions that blend challenging questions with humor, fostering a lively and supportive atmosphere. These gatherings encourage the exchange of knowledge and the development of quick thinking, all while building a sense of community among participants. By emphasizing that quizzing is an activity for everyone, the club dismantles barriers to participation, inviting all students to engage with and contribute to Ashoka's dynamic quizzing culture. Through its diverse initiatives, the Quizzing Club not only entertains but also enriches the intellectual fabric of the university, making learning an enjoyable and collective experience.

attributes.name: The Product Management Club
attributes.short_description: The Product Management Club at Ashoka University is a vibrant community dedicated to nurturing aspiring product managers and fostering a culture of innovation and leadership. Our mission is to equip students with the skills, knowledge, and networks necessary to excel in the dynamic field of product management.
attributes.description:
This year, the club has organized several impactful initiatives, including the Product Management Bootcamp, which offered participants a comprehensive exploration of the product lifecycle, customer-centric design principles, and the 0-to-1 product development process. The Bootcamp featured keynote speeches, panel discussions, a hands-on hackathon, and mentorship opportunities, enabling participants to gain practical experience and network with industry leaders.

Our club's verticals—Social Media, Outreach & Industry Connect, and Skills Development—drive our activities. Members have enhanced our online presence, built relationships with industry professionals and alumni, and designed workshops to equip peers with in-demand product management skills.

Guided by Ashoka University’s Career Development Office and mentored by Deep Kalra, Founder & Chairman of MakeMyTrip, the club aims to bridge the gap between academia and industry. We aspire to empower students to become future-ready leaders in product management, providing them with a platform for growth and collaboration.

attributes.name: Pawsitive
attributes.short_description: Pawsitive, Ashoka University’s student-led animal welfare club, is dedicated to improving the lives of street dogs and cats on campus. Our mission is to provide food, shelter, and medical care for these animals while fostering a compassionate community among students, faculty, and staff.\nThis year, our team continued feeding campus dogs twice daily, utilizing leftover mess food supplemented with dog food. We worked closely with local veterinarians and shelters to ensure injured animals received prompt medical care, including sterilization and vaccinations. To fund these efforts, we hosted multiple fundraisers and community engagement events.\nA major highlight was our collaboration with the Ministry of Community Well-Being for a special “meet-and-treat” event. Students and faculty bonded with the dogs, enjoyed their unique personalities, and experienced the joy of furry cuddles. The event emphasised the therapeutic benefits of interacting with animals as a way to relax and unwind.
attributes.description:
Pawsitive is the student-led animal welfare club of Ashoka University, dedicated to improving the lives of stray dogs and cats around the campus. Our mission is to provide food, shelter, and medical care for these animals while fostering a sense of community among the Ashoka students, faculty, and staff. At the heart of Pawsitive, we prioritize the welfare of the dogs, ensuring that all of our efforts are in their best interest.

Our team feeds the dogs twice a day, utilizing leftover food from the campus mess, supplemented with dog food and other dietary needs. Volunteers from the Ashokan community often join us during these feeding sessions. We maintain strong ties with local veterinarians and animal shelters, ensuring that injured animals receive prompt medical attention. To cover expenses for feeding, medical care, sterilization, and vaccinations, we organize several fundraisers.

Pawsitive also holds regular "meet-and-treat" events, where students and faculty can interact with the dogs, learn their names and unique personalities, and enjoy strolls filled with dog cuddles and kisses.

Recently, the club held a special "meet-and-treat" event in collaboration with the Ministry of Community Well-Being. Students had the opportunity to closely interact with the dogs, give them lots of treats, and play with them. This event was part of a project aimed at finding ways for people to unwind and relax—and what better way than to receive some furry cuddles!


The Ashokan community has been immensely supportive of Pawsitive. Recently, we had to launch a mass fundraising campaign for a campus dog named Stockings, who was severely injured. The entire Ashokan community—students, faculty, staff, and alumni—came together to pool funds for his treatment. We managed to raise over eighty thousand rupees in just a week. Apart from monetary donations, Pawsitive also received help with transportation, boarding facilities, and more. The way the community rallied together in Stockings' time of need was a testament to the incredible bond we share with these animals and with each other. It was a poignant reminder of why we do what we do and the impact we can make when we come together.


Pawsitive has an ever-expanding dog family and is looking to hold several fundraising events to ensure prompt care for the dogs. We also plan to create a repository of resources related to animal rescue and welfare, which will be available to the community. Students looking to get involved with Pawsitive can join our feeding sessions, assist with vet visits, and help organize events. We have an active WhatsApp group for coordinating volunteer efforts and responding to emergencies.

attributes.name: Orators Club
attributes.short_description: The Orators’ Club is a student-led initiative which was established in 2020 to foster a peer-learning platform for the student-body to support them through their oratory journey. The club’s motto is ‘Everything Speaking and In All Languages’. The club does not limit itself to public speaking, rather follows a much broader definition of oratory. The club aims to provide a platform for the students to display their oratory skills while giving them the support to improve their oratory skills. The Orators Club’s purpose is to provide a safe space for students to inculcate and grow their speaking skills, and become a confident version of themselves. By interacting with our different events and workshops, they are introduced to various forms of oratory and thereby are better equipped to display their oratory skills.
attributes.description:
The Orators’ Club at Ashoka University, founded in 2020, is a dynamic student-led initiative dedicated to creating a supportive, peer-driven platform where individuals can cultivate and showcase their oratory skills. Guided by its motto, "Everything Speaking and In All Languages," the club embraces a broad and inclusive approach to oratory that extends beyond traditional public speaking. It is a space for students to explore the art of communication in all its forms, whether through structured debates, storytelling, or impromptu speeches. The club’s mission is rooted in fostering a sense of confidence and self-expression, encouraging students to step out of their comfort zones and grow into compelling speakers.

 
The club curates a diverse array of workshops and events that introduce students to various dimensions of oratory. From parliamentary debate training to collaborative sessions blending persuasive speaking and negotiation tactics, the activities are designed to challenge and inspire participants. The Student Speaker Series stands out as a signature initiative, offering students a platform to share their personal narratives on thought-provoking themes, fostering a culture of storytelling and meaningful dialogue. Collaborations with external organizations further amplify the club’s impact, such as co-hosting the 'Viksit Bharat' debate, where students engaged with critical national issues alongside eminent speakers like Amitabh Kant, India’s G20 Sherpa. These events exemplify the club’s commitment to merging intellectual rigor with effective communication.

 
What sets the Orators’ Club apart is its emphasis on inclusivity and creativity. It invites students from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds to explore oratory as a universal skill. The club not only provides resources and mentorship but also cultivates a supportive community where members inspire one another. By engaging with the club’s initiatives, students gain exposure to varied forms of communication, from persuasive arguments to powerful storytelling, equipping them with the tools to articulate their ideas confidently in any setting. Through its vibrant activities and unwavering support, the Orators’ Club plays a transformative role in shaping Ashoka University’s community of thinkers, speakers, and leaders.

attributes.name: Neev: The Community Engagement Club
attributes.short_description: Neev is Ashoka's community engagement club that builds long-term, meaningful relationships between Ashokans and the residents of Asawarpur. We believe in working with the community, not just for it. With children, we run weekly teaching sessions for Classes 1-8, one-on-one and computer classes for high school students, and provide support for college applications, including Ashoka's. We also organize Friday playdates for the kids that combine joy and learning, giving children space to explore extracurricular activities. We also work with the community through projects like painting school walls and building the Neev Library. We also create platforms that connect Asawarpur with the Ashokan community: Neev Haat, which supports local vendors; Art Ashoka Asawarpur, which brings together children and Ashoka students through creativity; and The Late Late Night, our flagship fundraiser where professors join us for fun games and interactions.

attributes.name: Mad Batter
attributes.short_description: They say too many cooks spoil the broth, but at Mad Batter, it’s the opposite—our club thrives on the collective creativity and passion of food enthusiasts across campus. Whether you’re an experienced baker or a complete beginner, there’s a place for you in our warm, welcoming community.
attributes.description:
Mad Batter isn’t just about baking or cooking; it’s about experimenting, exploring, and connecting through food. This year, we’ve hosted a variety of events, from selling PupCakes for Pawsitive’s fundraiser to crafting trifles at Zehen, Psych Haat’24. Our festive stalls have been a hit too, featuring Cake Pops on Halloween, Dhokla on Garba Night, and Chocolate and Cookie Fudge at Noor-e-Jazbaa.

Looking ahead, we’re gearing up for our Valentine Wonderland event. From decadent desserts to delightful pairings, with this event we promise to bring a little extra magic to campus as we mix love and confections into a perfect recipe.

The heart of Mad Batter lies in the joy of trying something new—whether it’s perfecting your piping skills, learning (or failing at) the art of tempering chocolate, or simply sharing stories while whipping cream by hand for hours. We believe food has the power to bridge differences and create bonds that last beyond the kitchen.


Join us as we whip, fold, and bake our way through the semester—you’ll always have a seat at our table!
attributes.induction_description:
We are Ashoka's baking and cooking club and love all things food. So if food is what you are about, we are for you. Whether you are an amateur or a pro, it doesn’t matter— everyone is welcome! With us, you can expect to participate in the oddest club traditions (you will know soon, if inducted), turn those late-night baking dreams into reality, and have a blast in the chaos that is our team! We are thrilled at the thought of you joining us in on this chaos and cannot wait to hear the amazing ideas you will bring to the table. The induction process consists of a written application, followed by an interview for the shortlisted candidates.

What you can apply for:

1. Member:

This is for ANYONE that’s interested in being part of Mad Batter - someone who enjoys food, late night baking sessions and of course, eating. As a member, you’d be part of planning and executing events hosted by us. You would take part in brainstorming discussions to come up with dishes and recipes and then sign up for slots for various tasks. These would include baking, setting up, wrapping up, selling and documenting events. 

What you need: A genuine eagerness to cook/bake as a community, brainstorm recipes and ideas, and sell our treats to the student body. Past experience is NOT necessary and you are encouraged to apply and learn with the rest of us. 

2. Social Media POC:

As the social media POC, your responsibilities would differ from the general member. While you are welcome to participate in the aforementioned activities, your primary role would be to work towards the marketing and the online presence of Mad Batter. This would mainly include ideating, filming and posting for Instagram through reels and posts. 

What you need: Fun, trendy ideas to make posts on Instagram. Prior experience in basic designing is great but not necessary. Apply if you think you’d be a good fit!

Apply now: https://forms.gle/5ZWib9Se9aqAD3vXA

 

PS- If you don't want to formally join the club but would like to stay updated on events, workshops and volunteer opportunities, you can use this link to join a community of fellow food lovers. Here is the WhatsApp link: https://chat.whatsapp.com/GB1zLWD4aWBBea6zn9LHkJ

attributes.name: Lang-Up
attributes.short_description: Lang-up, the language club of Ashoka University, is a vibrant community that brings together students with a shared passion for languages and cultures
attributes.description: The club operates through diverse language columns, each fostering the exploration and appreciation of a specific language. Students can join these columns to deepen their interests or even start new ones to enhance the presence of a language on campus. Throughout the year, Lang-up organizes engaging activities, including language-learning workshops and movie screenings. These initiatives create a welcoming space for enthusiasts to connect, share, and learn together. Whether you're a polyglot or just starting to explore a new language, Lang-up offers an inclusive platform to discover the joy of multilingualism and cross-cultural appreciation.

attributes.name: Kalinga
attributes.short_description: Kalinga Magazine is the official satire magazine of Ashoka University, where we keep abreast with current campus events, politics, student ongoings and administrative news and discuss relevant issues across the Ashokan bubble through the medium of satire.
attributes.description:
We have the following departments: Editorial, Illustrations, Multimedia & Marketing and Campus Events & Collaborations (CEC). The last department, CEC was launched in Monsoon 2024 during the inductions in an effort to expand our campus engagements. Kalinga is where writers, illustrators, designers, videographers and more come together, cross-departmentally to collaborate on pieces for each magazine issue as the primary goal of the magazine.

This last year, 2024 onwards, aside from participating in the Cul-Min mandated events such as Jazbaa and Clubs & Socs Fair, our team has put out articles for editions, collaborated with Ashoka Public Policy Society for a Policy Parody Competition and relaunched our social media to increase our engagements.

attributes.name: Iron Eagles
attributes.short_description: The Iron Eagles is Ashoka University's premier fitness, health, and gym club. We aim to build a strong community centred around powerlifting, strength training, and overall well-being. Our events celebrate physical endurance, mental resilience, and inclusivity, ensuring every student finds a space to thrive. This year, we hosted flagship events like the Bench Press Competition, where participants showcased their strength in AMRAP (As Many Reps As Possible) and One-Rep Max categories. Collaborating with brands like The Whole Truth and community clubs like the Sports Enthusiasts Community (SEC) ensured safety, fun, and memorable experiences for all. Other highlights include our Push-Up and Weight Hold Challenges and the introduction of Non-Cis Men Hours, which foster a safer and more inclusive gym environment. Through these initiatives, alongside our Instagram Healthy Eating series and collaborations with brands and campus clubs, we continue to inspire students to lead healthier lives and push past their limits.
attributes.description:
The Iron Eagles is more than just a fitness club; it is a vibrant community dedicated to empowering Ashoka students through strength training, fitness education, and holistic well-being. Our mission is to foster both physical and mental resilience while cultivating a spirit of inclusivity, collaboration, and community.

Over the past semester, Iron Eagles organized flagship events like the Bench Press Competition and Push-Up Challenges, attracting hundreds of spectators and participants. We also introduced Non-Cis Men Hours at the gym, creating a safer and more inclusive space for women and non-cis men to engage in fitness activities. These initiatives, along with collaborations with brands like The Whole Truth and events at fests such as SHATRANJ, have solidified Iron Eagles’ reputation as a dynamic and impactful student organization.

Looking ahead to Spring 2025, we aim to elevate our impact through new initiatives. Planned highlights include specialized workshops on injury prevention and self-defence, a triathlon, and innovative challenges like the 1-Week Vegan Challenge and the 30-Day Flexibility Challenge. To enhance gym inclusivity, we will expand Non-Cis Men Hours and organize compound lift workshops with the female trainer at the gym.

attributes.name: Anitya: the Social Impact Club
attributes.short_description:
"Anitya, the Social Impact Club, aims to foster meaningful community dialogue around social impact and empower students and leaders to create value in their communities and organizations. Serving as a platform to connect students, organizations, and professionals in the social impact sector, the club provides educational, experiential, and networking opportunities for its members. Anitya strives to bridge the gap between the Ashokan student body and the social impact sector by offering career growth opportunities through diverse initiatives. These include disseminating knowledge through expert speaker sessions, talks, and newsletters; facilitating off-campus exposure via field visits, internships, and networking opportunities; and creating additional spaces on campus for engagement through events such as case competitions, ideathons, and student discussions.
Additionally, Anitya supports social sector organizations by connecting them with the Ashokan community, providing them a platform to expand their presence, onboard passionate interns, and engage with the youth. We also aim to conduct on-ground impact projects, driving actual change by uplifting communities.
In the past year, the club has hosted several impactful events, including our flagship Development Sector Bootcamp – where we hosted 8 expert leaders in the social sector – in collaboration with the CDO, a concert for the housekeeping staff in collaboration with the NGO Manzil Mystics, and various stalls supporting NGOs like Nepathya and Goonj. Other initiatives include Swades, a case competition with UpkramEdu, and an internship program with V All."
attributes.description:
Anitya, the Social Impact Club, is dedicated to fostering a culture of both dialogue and action around social impact. The club envisions creating a vibrant ecosystem where students, professionals, and organizations in the social impact sector can collaborate to generate meaningful value in their communities and beyond. With an emphasis on educational, experiential, and networking opportunities, Anitya serves as a bridge connecting the Ashokan student body with the larger social impact landscape.
At its core, Anitya’s mission is to empower students to explore career paths and initiatives that align with the values of social responsibility and sustainable impact. To achieve this, the club provides a wide range of opportunities and resources, ensuring that members develop a comprehensive understanding of the social impact space. These efforts are structured around three key pillars: knowledge and information dissemination, on-ground exposure, and campus engagement. By hosting speaker sessions, talks, and workshops, the club equips members with the knowledge needed to navigate the complexities of social impact work. We provide on-ground exposure to students through field visits, internships, community projects, and networking opportunities. As for the last pillar of campus engagement, we do so by conducting exciting value-adding events like case competitions and ideathons, creating a platform for students to actively participate in addressing social impact themes.


Furthermore, the club supports various social organizations by helping them expand their presence within the Ashokan community. By organizing stalls, events, and internships, Anitya facilitates meaningful connections between students and organizations, fostering a mutually beneficial relationship that empowers young changemakers.


Over the past year, Anitya has organized several impactful events and initiatives. Our flagship event was the Development Sector Bootcamp, conducted in collaboration with the Career Development Office (CDO). The bootcamp featured prominent sector leaders including Urvashi Prasad (director at NITI Aayog), Pramath Raj Sinha (Founding Dean at ISB & Founder at Harappa), and Shoikat Roy (Core Member at the Punjab Development Commission). The club also hosted a concert for the entire housekeeping staff, in collaboration with the organization 'Manzil Mystics'. Other initiatives included collaborations with Nepathya NGO to sell clothes made by women from Sikkim and a book sale with Goonj in collaboration with Epigraph, supporting meaningful causes while fostering community engagement. Other highlights also include Swades, a case competition held in collaboration with UpkramEdu, and an internship orientation program with the organization V All.


Through these initiatives, Anitya continues to inspire and support students to explore the social impact space, fostering a culture of responsible thinking, innovation and collaboration. As we move forward, we will continue to build on these programs and carry out impactful and value-adding initiatives.
